`src/commands.ts` imports only zod. Sketch:
```ts
type Effect = 'logged'|'corrected'|'deleted'|'undone'|'remembered'|'forgotten'|'reminded'|'unreminded'
interface Entry {
  input: z.ZodObject<any>               // domain input: optional fields, unions, no `text`, no sentinels; .max() bounds and .describe() live here
  kind: 'read'|'write'|'answer'|'ask'
  effect?: Effect                        // writes only; replaces CHANGES, KIND_OF_TOOL, Applied
  label: 'log'|'correct'|'delete'|'undo'|'remember'|'forget'|'remind'|'summarize'|'ask'|'reply'|'link'|'disconnect'|'find'
  alone?: true                           // undo_last, forget_all_facts, reply

  mcp?: { name: `warren_${string}`; title: string; description: string; destructive: boolean }
}                                        // neither agent nor mcp = code-only (notice, link_*, mcp_disconnect, forget_all_confirmed)
export const COMMANDS = { ... } as const satisfies Record<string, Entry>
export type Command = { [N in Name]: { tool: N; input: z.infer<(typeof COMMANDS)[N]['input']> } }[Name]
export type WriteCommand = Extract<Command, { tool: NamesWhere<'write'> }>
```

What stays outside: guards (calls.ts), apply (apply.ts), render (render.ts) and MCP present stay as `switch` over the `Command` or `Outcome` union, with `never` exhaustiveness. redesign.problem: 12 tools carry `text: Say()` (src/agent/schema.ts:165-212) and the machinery to police it is the regex half of say.ts: CLAIMS (say.ts:114-185), FILLER and restates (291-311), echoes (279-288), KIND_OF_TOOL and Applied (80-105), the per-action verdict loop and the set_reminder special case (466-524), plus in the loop amountsOf, textFlaws and the repair branches (src/agent/loop.ts:12-24, 206-232, 365-399). say.ts was touched by every feature slice after it was written (git log: +31 voice, +12 undo, +65 memory, +29 reminders). The stored runs say the text is noise.
redesign.proposal: Remove `text` from every action tool. Keep `reply({text})` with the numbers check (tokens, made-of-pieces, 280 characters) and the claims check. Add one terminal tool: `skip: z.object({ part: z.string().min(1).max(60), reason: z.enum(['not_found','cannot_do','send_apart']) })`, kind 'answer'. Guard: `unwritten(part, message)` is empty and every word of `part` is a word of the person's message (the rule facts already use for a key, src/agent/memory.ts:172-177), so no regex list guards it. Code renders one plain line per reason. A part that needs detail (`cambiame el primero`) is `ask_user` on that id with after_answer none, not a text: today the prompt asks for a free-text question (src/agent/prompt.ts:139) which stores no `asked` or `pending`, so the person's next bare answer cannot be resolved by code (src/resolve.ts:80-100). A doubtful amount or category is already `confidence: 'low'` and the `(?)` mark (src/render.ts:178). For `reply`, the claims check reads the turn's effects from the registry and the window's effects from the turn table council 1 decided, instead of the ten `window:` regexes over render.ts wording (the dependency say.ts:107-113 admits). Fallback if the eval rejects `skip`: let `reply` stand beside writes for the part not done and keep `restates`; still one free-text channel instead of 13. Option (c) is rejected: it reverses the owner's 'code renders every record', the check only proves where a number came from, not which movement it belongs to (agent-spec.md B2 notes, 'What it does not do'), and Haiku 5.5 with thinking off is the configuration the docs tie to reasoning-like text in replies.
redesign.evidence: Of 2,591 calls to tools that have a text field, 173 (6.7%) carried one and 68 (2.6%) reached the person; 105 were dropped by code. By tool (calls / with text / sent): summarize 392/57/0, all echoes of the question; delete_movement 477/41/13; remember_fact 112/45/28; log_movements 752/24/24; correct_movement 710/3/3; forget_fact 19/3/0; undo_last 67/0/0; list_facts 46/0/0; forget_all_facts 16/0/0. The 68 sent, by a regex classification of mine: 29 restate the record (`Anotado: el sueldo te cae el 28.` beside the code line; scenarios s117, s167, s169, s182), 29 are questions from three scenarios (s012 `kiosco 15`, where code already prints `(?)`; s096; s171), 6 are not-found or not-done lines (s096, s117, s171), 4 other. So the content worth keeping is exactly what `skip` and `ask_user` carry. 20 audit entries are `repair` (a whole extra model turn): reply 11, log_movements 7, correct_movement 2; the 9 on writes disappear by construction. The loop's own messages tell the model to write `Mandame lo otro aparte.` as text (src/agent/loop.ts:175,177): that is `skip` with reason send_apart.

redesign.measure: Rerun the baseline on main first (214 scenarios now). Then `pnpm eval:scenarios --split dev` three times and ten targeted reruns of s068-s073, s096, s117, s012, s171, s112. Must show: fully right within the usual 2-scenario band of baseline, 0 silent wrong changes, 0 invented numbers, 0 unnecessary questions, second-model-turn rate not above the 4.0% of the speed pass (8 of 201), and in every multi-part scenario the part not done appears as a `skip` line or a question. redesign.item: 3. Clean canonical input schemas: real optionals, a typed range, no placeholders; MCP shares them
redesign.problem: The shapes were written for strict limits that no longer bind (src/agent/schema.ts:62-69 says so). The model writes null, "" and 0 on every call, and the placeholders cause refusals, each a full extra model turn (about 0.8-1.2 s, agent-spec.md:916). They also reach MCP clients: `a field a period does not use stays 0 or ""` (src/mcp/tools.ts:351), the `other` mini-language (src/mcp/tools.ts:375-381). MCP then re-declares the write schemas anyway (src/mcp/write-tools.ts:59-94) and maps back to placeholders: `id ?? 0, key ?? ''`, `text: null`, `confidence: 'high'` (write-tools.ts:153,173,189,206,234,255).
redesign.proposal: One schema per tool with `.describe()` on fields, used by both channels. Range = z.discriminatedUnion('period', [ {period: z.enum(NAMED_PERIODS)}, {period: 'month', month: 1..12, year?: int}, {period: 'year', year: int}, {period: 'dates', from: string, to?: string} ]). summarize = { range: Range, group_by?: GROUPS (default none), compare?: 'previous' | Range, direction?, category?, payment?, description? }: one field replaces compare_to + other, so two fields can no longer disagree, and parseOther goes. forget_fact = { id?: positive int, key?: string }, exactly one, checked in code as today (calls.ts:198). Movement.payment optional; `confidence` default high and omitted over MCP. ask_user = { movement_ids, after_answer, changes? } without `question`: code picks the phrase from after_answer and the number of options. Emit with `z.toJSONSchema(schema, { io: 'input' })` minus `$schema`, which I checked drops defaulted fields from `required`; this replaces the hand `strip` (src/agent/tools.ts:38-52). MCP-only fields (request_id, limit, cursor) come from `mcp.extra`.
redesign.evidence: Of the 24 guard refusals in the data (not counting 16 'no tool call'), 14 are placeholder artifacts: ask_user `changes.amount: amount ""` 7 (s126-s128), summarize `other is only for compare_to "range"` 4 on plain queries such as `cuanto voy este mes` (s081, s084, s113), forget_fact both-or-neither 3 (s182). 8 more are ask_user correct-without-changes. ask_user.question over 481 calls: `Cuál` 268, `Cuál café y qué cambio` 101, `Qué querés cambiar` 88, the other 24 are `cuál <noun> y qué ...` variants, so the field is derivable and cleanQuestion (calls.ts:94-102) guards a text channel nobody needs. forget_fact was by id in 19 of 19 calls. Query is the action with the most output tokens (257-261 per turn, agent-spec.md:1006), carrying 9 always-present fields; 11 prompt examples carry the full placeholder range.

Prompt examples shrink by about 1 KB.
redesign.measure: Dev scenarios three times plus `pnpm eval --split dev`. Must show: query and summary tags at baseline (18/18 and 17/17 in the last stored all-run), summarize refusals at or below today's 4 of 392 calls, the three placeholder refusal reasons at 0, mean output tokens per query lower. Reject the typed range if summarize refusals rise (the model mixing fields across union branches without strict) or the query tag loses more than one scenario. verdict: adjust. The loop's shape is right and I would build it the same way today: a hand-written loop, terminal tools, nothing written before the commit point, writes held when the same turn searched (src/agent/loop.ts:186-191, 358-381). What I would not rebuild is how the guards are laid out. checkCall and valueGuards are two parallel switches that agree only by convention, and turn-level rules are split between the loop and the guard. Code-made declines travel as a 'notice' whose text is later string-compared to decide redaction, and three text rules about the person's message have crept back in (namesTodayAtATime, hasValue, 'el último'). On the 1.5-turn question I reject the id-or-match proposal: a wrong single match chosen by code is a silent wrong change under the gate. A code pre-search placed in the context gets the same one-turn result while the model still picks the id with the rows in view. The scenario eval cannot measure either option today: only 8 non-summary scenarios seed 10 or more movements, so long-ledger scenarios must come first.

redesign.item: Clarifying questions at 1.5 model turns: a code pre-search in the context instead of id-or-match on correct/delete/ask_user
redesign.problem: Tools take only an id, so anything outside the 10 newest rows costs a search turn. The proposed match {text,date?,amount?,payment?} resolved by code moves the pick from the model to a substring query: src/ledger.ts:358-371 uses LIKE '%word%', so 'café' matches 'Cafetera'. A single wrong hit that code acts on is a wrong write under a '✓' reply, which evals/scenarios/grade.ts:321 counts as a silent wrong change. Match also needs new outcomes (ambiguous, none), a way to express 'el X fue N: log it if nothing matches', and a bypass of the shown-ids guard. On a synonym miss it still takes a second turn, so it only wins where a lexical match exists.
redesign.proposal: Keep ids only. Before the model call, in the existing Promise.all (src/process.ts:267-272), add mentionedMovements(sql, accountId, message, {excludeIds: newest10, limit: 8}): live rows beyond the newest 10 where a folded word of 4+ letters of the description or payment is a word of the folded message, or the amount equals a number written in the message. Render them as a block: 'Más antiguos que nombra este mensaje (ya buscados por sus palabras): id=… …', or '(ninguno)' when the ledger has 10 or more rows. Add their ids to the shown set. find_movements stays for dates and synonyms. This is retrieval, not intent: code decides nothing, and facts already work this way (src/facts.ts:31-54, MAX_MATCHED_FACTS). With stable entity ids nothing else changes, and MCP is unaffected. If match is still wanted afterwards, allow it only on ask_user, where the worst case is a poor list of options, never a write.
redesign.evidence: Only 8 non-summary scenarios of 214 seed 10+ movements (s028, s067, s075-s078, s098, s117). In the 8 newest stored all-split result files, 27 of 1,300 model turns used find_movements and 3 of 170 ask turns followed a search, while live asks average 1.5 turns (task brief). The eval therefore does not reproduce the live cause. The complete-list line (prompt.ts:575-579) already removed the search for ledgers under 10 rows by telling the model there is nothing more to find. Pre-search extends the same idea to long ledgers.
redesign.size: +70 lines (query, context block, wiring, one prompt rule), about +15 scenarios; no schema change
redesign.confidence: medium-high that it is safer than match; medium on how much of the live 1.5 turns it removes, because I could not read live tool_calls
redesign.measure: First add about 15 long-ledger scenarios (12-40 seeded rows): older item named exactly, by synonym, by date, by amount, several matches (ask), no match (ask or log), and plain logs that share a word with an older row. Baseline them, then compare. Adopt if there are 0 silent wrong changes, 0 invented numbers, existing dev stays within the ±2 scenario noise, and the second-turn rate on the new set at least halves. Reject if a plain log becomes a correction or a question even once in 3 runs, or if model p50 rises more than 100 ms.

redesign.item: Guards by construction: one entry per tool with values() and an optional conversation(), a turn-level checkTurn, and a typed 'declined' result
redesign.problem: checkCall and valueGuards are two switches over the same tool names with casts (calls.ts:137-220 and 294-378). The conversation layer re-implements log (304-313 against 163-169), delete (318-322) and remember (325-336) instead of wrapping the value layer. The value layer takes the conversation's message (calls.ts:133, 209). Turn-level state is split: the loop bumps guard.logged (loop.ts:325-326), the guard mutates guard.remembered (calls.ts:331-334), and the alone rule sits in the loop (loop.ts:345-354). A code-made decline is returned as kind 'action' with a notice text (calls.ts:244-267), so MCP special-cases it (src/mcp/write-tools.ts:113) and redaction is decided by comparing that text to a canned reply (src/redact.ts:15-16, process.ts:429). The loop also runs code's own notice through the model-text check, because a Notice has 'text' in its input (loop.ts:220-230); it passes today only because of its wording.
redesign.proposal: Checked = read | action | declined {why: 'secret'|'contact'|'reminder_past'|'reminder_far'} | rejected {message}. A registry entry is {name, kind: read|write|answer|ask, alone?: string, input: zod, values(input, {today, now}) → Checked, conversation?(input, turn) → Checked | null}. checkValues(name, input, env) is what MCP calls (today's checkInput). checkTurn(calls, turn) → Checked[] runs conversation then values per call, then the set rules in one pure function: at most 10 movements across calls, one value per fact key, alone. Turn = {shown: {movements, facts, reminders}, message, sole, today, now}. A notice carries a code, not a text: {tool:'notice', input:{code}}, rendered by render.ts. Redaction is then code === 'secret', and the loop's text check cannot see notices.

redesign.item: Reminder time: the model says what the person said, code resolves it; delete namesTodayAtATime

'En 45 minutos' is clock arithmetic by the model, and a time of today that has passed was moved to tomorrow in about 3 of 8 runs (reminders-spec, 'A time of today that has passed'). The fix was a regex over the person's message (calls.ts:235-241, 337-353) that overrides the model's schedule. A pure resolveFirst(first, now) → {start, time} | 'past' sits beside nextOccurrence; {day:'today'} with a passed time is 'past' by structure and code never rolls a named day. The stored Schedule, send.ts, describe.ts and undo are unchanged. Split the guard: checkReminderValues(input, now) for any sender, and a conversation rule (numbers in what are the person's; a secret in the message) for WhatsApp.

The frozen tools+system prefix sits under one 1h breakpoint (loop.ts:136-148), and the volatile context goes in the first user turn with the newest date (prompt.ts:567). range.ts resolves days in code with correct Argentine semantics. In the registry entry:
```ts
const Range = () => z.discriminatedUnion('period', [
  z.object({ period: z.enum(NAMED_PERIODS) }),
  z.object({ period: z.literal('month'), month: z.number().int(), year: z.number().int().optional() }),
  z.object({ period: z.literal('year'), year: z.number().int() }),
  z.object({ period: z.literal('last_days'), days: z.number().int() }), // 'los últimos 30 días', code: today-(days-1)..today

])
summarize: z.object({
  range: Range(),
  group_by: z.enum(GROUPS).default('none'),
  compare: z.union([z.literal('previous'), Range()]).optional(), // absent = no comparison
  direction: Direction().optional(), category: Category().optional(),
  payment: z.string().optional(), description: z.string().optional(),
})
```

RangeSchema = z.discriminatedUnion('period', [
  z.strictObject({ period: z.enum(NAMED_PERIODS) }),
  z.strictObject({ period: z.literal('month'), month: z.number().int(), year: z.number().int().optional() }),
  z.strictObject({ period: z.literal('year'), year: z.number().int() }),
  z.strictObject({ period: z.literal('dates'), from: z.string(), to: z.string().optional() }),
])

summarize = z.object({ range: RangeSchema, group_by: z.enum(GROUPS).optional(), compare: z.union([z.literal('previous'), RangeSchema]).optional(), direction, category, payment, description: all optional })
